Surah al-Jathiyah

Makkiyyah, and it has thirty-seven verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Ha-Mim.﴾ The discussion of this is as has passed in the opening of Surah al-Mu'min. If it is made a name for the surah, then its place in the i'rab (grammatical analysis) is the nominative, as it is a predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: this is named "Ha-Mim." The reference to the surah before its mention has passed has been explained to you repeatedly, and its secret you have come to know. If it is taken as a mere enumeration of letters in the manner of listing, then it has no share in i'rab.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 2:

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾, according to the first view it is a predicate following another predicate, on the basis that it is a verbal noun (masdar) used in the sense of the object (maf'ul) for emphasis (mubalaghah). According to the second view, it is the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada' mudmar) which the preceding words hint at, meaning: what is composed of the kind of what has been mentioned is "the revelation of the Book." It has also been said that it is the predicate of "Ha-Mim" (hamm), meaning: the one named by it is "the revelation of..." etc. It has been stated many times that what is made the title of a topic should be something whose attribution to it is already known beforehand; since there is no prior acquaintance with the naming at this point, its proper role is to be reported. As for making it a predicate of "Ha-Mim" by supposing an omitted genitive (mudaf) and keeping "revelation" in its original sense, i.e., "the revelation of Ha-Mim is the revelation of the Book," then, despite its being free of conveying any worthwhile benefit, it is a forced interpretation (tamahhul).

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾, it was explained in detail at the beginning of surah al-Zumar. It has been said: ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ is an oath by which Allah swears, "the revelation of the Book" is its attribute, and the answer to the oath is His saying, the Exalted:

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.﴾ And this, according to the aforementioned modes, is a resumptive statement (kalam mustaʾnaf), brought in to draw attention to the cosmic signs (al-ayat al-takwiniyya), both those of the horizons (al-afaqiyya) and those within the self (al-anfusiyya). The locus of the signs is either the heavens and the earth themselves, for they encompass, among the varieties of signs, what expression falls short of describing; or it is their creation, as in His exalted saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, and this is more fitting with His exalted saying:

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 4:

﴿And in your creation﴾, i.e., from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, passing through various and differing stages until the creation is complete.

﴿And what He scatters of living creatures (dabba)﴾ is a conjunction with the thing being added to (al-mudaf), not the thing it is added to (al-mudaf ilayhi); i.e., and in what He spreads abroad and disperses of living creatures.

﴿Signs﴾ is in the nominative (raf'), being the subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is the fronted adverbial phrase (al-zarf al-muqaddam), and the sentences are conjoined to what precedes them, the sentence introduced by inna (indeed). It is said: "signs" is conjoined to the preceding "signs" by virtue of its position (al-mahall), according to those who permit this. It was also read "sign" (ayah) in the singular, and it was read "signs" (ayat) in the accusative, conjoined to what precedes it, namely the noun of inna and its predicate, as if it were said: "Indeed, in your creation and in what He scatters of living creatures are signs."

﴿For a people who have certainty﴾, i.e., it is characteristic of them to be certain of things as they actually are.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 5:

﴿And the alternation of the night and the day﴾ is in the genitive case (bi-l-jarr), on the supposition of the preposition mentioned in the two verses before it. It has also been read with the mention of the preposition ("bi-dhikrihinna"). The intended meaning is: "by the alternation of the two," either their succession (ta'aqub) or their difference in length and shortness.

﴿And what Allah sends down from the sky﴾ is conjoined (ʿatf) to "alternation" (ikhtilaf).

﴿of provision﴾, that is, of rain, which is a cause of provision. It is expressed by this to draw attention to its being a sign from the two aspects of power and mercy.

﴿and gives life thereby to the earth﴾ by bringing forth from it kinds of crops, fruits, and plants.

﴿after its death﴾ and its barrenness, being devoid of the traces of life, the absence of the power of growth in it, and its trees being empty of fruit.

﴿and the turning of the winds﴾ from one direction to another and from one state to another. It has also been read as "al-rih" (the singular). Its being mentioned after the sending down of rain, although it precedes it in existence, is either to signify that it is an independent sign—for if the existential order had been observed, it might have been supposed that the combination of the turning of the winds and the sending down of rain was a single sign—or because the turning of the winds being a sign is not merely because it is the origin of the producing of rain, but because of it and of the other benefits, among which is the driving of ships in the seas.

﴿are signs for a people who use their reason﴾. It is read in the nominative (raf') on the basis that it is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is the preceding prepositional phrase, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. It has also been read in the accusative (nasb) on the basis of specification (ikhtisas). It was said: it is the noun of "inna," and the genitive phrase mentioned earlier is its predicate by way of conjunction to the two operands of two different governing elements, namely "inna" and "fi," the waw having been placed in their stead; so it governed the genitive in "ikhtilaf" and the accusative in "ayat." The indefiniteness of "ayat" in the three positions is for magnification, both in quantity and in quality, and the variation of the rhyme endings (fawasil) is due to the difference in the levels of the signs in subtlety and clarity.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 6:

﴿These are the signs of Allah⁠﴾ is a subject and predicate (mubtada' and khabar). His saying, exalted is He, ﴿We recite them to you⁠﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal), whose operative element is the meaning of the demonstrative (al-ishara). It has also been said that ﴿We recite them to you⁠﴾ is the predicate, and "the signs of Allah" is a substitute (badal) or an explanatory apposition ('atf bayan).

﴿In truth⁠﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to the doer of "We recite" (the subject) and to its object, meaning: We recite them while being truthful, or while they are connected with truth.

﴿Then in what discourse⁠﴾ means: among the discourses (al-ahadith).

﴿After Allah and His signs⁠﴾ means: after the signs of Allah. The placing of the Divine Name first is to magnify them, as in the saying "Zayd's generosity pleased me, and his generosity..." Or it means: after "the discourse of Allah," which is the Qur'an, as indicated by His saying, exalted is He, ﴿He has sent down the best discourse⁠﴾, and this is what is meant by "His signs." The basis of the conjunction is the difference in designation (al-taghayur al-'unwani).

﴿They believe⁠﴾ is in the third-person form (bi-sighat al-ghaybah), and it has also been read with the ta' (second-person form).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 7:

﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾ (every liar).

﴿Sinful﴾ (one who commits many sins).

﴿Who hears the verses of God﴾ is another attribute of "liar" (*affak*). It was also said that it is a resumptive sentence (*isti'naf*), and that it is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) from the pronoun in "sinner" (*athim*).

﴿Being recited to him﴾ is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) from "the verses of God." There is no basis for making it a second object of "hears," because the condition for that is that what follows should be something not heard, as in your saying: "I heard Zayd reciting" (*yaqra'u*).

﴿Then he persists﴾ means he remains in his disbelief. Its root is from the persistence of a donkey upon its herd of wild asses (*anah*).

﴿Arrogantly﴾ means refusing to believe in what he heard of the verses of God, and refusing to submit to what they say, looking down on them and being pleased with the falsehoods he has. It was also said that it was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who used to buy the tales of non-Arabs (*a'ajim*) and occupy people with them away from listening to the Qur'an. However, it came in general wording, censuring him and everyone who follows his course, and the evil and corruption they are in. The word "then" (*thumma*) expresses the improbability of persistence and arrogance after hearing verses that by right should make hearts submit and necks bow, as in the saying of the one who said: [He sees the throes of death, then he visits them].

﴿As if he had not heard it﴾ means as if he had not heard it. It is a lightened form, with the pronoun of the matter (*damir al-sha'n*) omitted, and the clause is a circumstantial clause from "persists," meaning: he persists, resembling one who did not hear.

﴿So give him the good news of a painful punishment﴾ for his persistence and his arrogance.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (*Irshād al-'Aql al-Salīm*) on Surah 45, Verse 9:**

﴿And when he learns anything of Our signs﴾. That is: when something of Our signs reaches him and he knows that it is from Our signs, not that he knows it as it truly is, for then he is far removed from that knowledge. It is also said: when he learns from them something that the obstinate person can cling to, and finds for it a corrupt interpretation (*maḥmal*) through which he reaches criticism and fault-finding.

﴿takes them﴾, that is, the signs, all of them.

﴿as a mockery﴾, that is, mocked by them, not only what he has heard. It is also said: the pronoun refers to *shay'* (thing), and the feminine form is because it carries the meaning of *al-āyāt* (the signs).

﴿Those﴾ is a reference to every *affāk* (liar, fabricator) in terms of being characterized by the vile traits mentioned. The plural is in view of the inclusiveness of all of them, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Every party rejoices in what it has﴾. Likewise, the singular in the pronouns previously mentioned is in view of each individual one.

﴿For them﴾, because of their aforementioned crimes.

﴿is a humiliating punishment﴾. The description of the punishment as humiliating is to fulfil the due of their arrogance and their mockery of the signs of God, glorified and exalted is He.

From behind them is Hell (jahannam), that is, in front of them, since they are turned toward what has been prepared for them; or behind them, since they turn away from that and devote themselves to this world. For "waraʾ" (behind/beyond) is a name for the direction that a person conceals from himself, whether behind or in front.

﴿And will not avail them﴾ means: will not avert.

﴿Whatever they earned﴾ of wealth and children.

﴿Anything﴾ of the punishment of God, the Exalted, or anything of enrichment.

﴿Nor those they took as protectors apart from God﴾ — that is, the idols. The placing of the negative particle between the two conjoined items, although the non-benefit of the idols is clearer and more evident than the non-benefit of wealth and children, is based on their corrupt assumption, since they used to hope for their intercession. And in this there is mockery.

﴿And for them﴾ in what lies beyond them of Hell:

﴿a great punishment﴾ whose magnitude cannot be measured.

This is the Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on Surah 45, verse 11:

﴿This﴾ i.e., the Qur'an.

﴿is guidance﴾ of the utmost perfection in guiding, as if it were guidance itself.

﴿And those who disbelieve﴾ i.e., in the Qur'an. He placed, in the position of its pronoun, His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿in the signs of their Lord﴾ to increase the reprehensibility of their disbelief in it and the monstrousness of their condition.

﴿For them is a punishment of painful wrath﴾ i.e., of the most severe punishment.

﴿painful﴾ is with the nominative (raf') as an adjective of "punishment" (ʿadhāb). It has also been read with the genitive (jarr), as an adjective of "rijz". The tanwin of "ʿadhāb" in the three positions is for emphasis (tafkhim), and its nominative case is either as the subject (mubtada') or as the agent (fa'iliyyah).

Abu al-Su'ud's Commentary (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on Surah 45, verse 12:

(p-70) ﴿Allah is He who subjected the sea for you﴾, by making its surface smooth, so that what floats on it, such as wood, rides upon it, and its smoothness does not prevent diving or piercing through it.

﴿That the ships may sail upon it by His command﴾, while you are riding them.

﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾ through trade, diving, hunting and other things.

﴿And that perhaps you may give thanks﴾, and that you may give thanks for the blessings that result from that.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 13:

﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ of existing things, by making them a means of benefit for you.

﴿All of it﴾ may be either a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of "whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth," or an emphatic restatement (tawkīd) of it.

﴿From Him﴾ is connected to an omitted element which is either a description of "all of it," or a circumstantial qualifier of "whatever" — meaning: all of it being from Him, exalted is He; or: He has subjected these things to you as beings originating from Him, created by Him, exalted is He; or it is a predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: they are all from Him, exalted is He. It has also been read as "minhu" as an object of purpose (maf'ūl lahu) and "minhu" as the agent of "subjected" (sakhkhara) by metaphorical attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī), or as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: that is from Him.

﴿Indeed, in that﴾ means: in what has been mentioned of the great matters.

﴿There are indeed signs﴾ of great importance and vast number.

﴿For a people who reflect﴾ upon the wondrous workmanship of God Most High, for by this they come to know the magnificent and subtle blessings of God Most High, and they are granted success in giving thanks for them.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 14:

﴿Say to those who believe﴾ The verb of saying (al-maqul) is omitted, due to the indication of what follows it.

﴿they should forgive﴾ Upon it (i.e., the command) depends the response (jawab) to the imperative, taken in relation to its being dependent on it, not merely in itself. That is: "Say to them: forgive, and they will forgive."

﴿those who do not expect the Days of Allah﴾ That is: they should pardon and overlook those who do not anticipate His events against His enemies, from the expression of the Arabs, "ayyam al-'Arab" (the days of the Arabs), for their battles. It was also said: those who do not hope for the times which Allah, exalted is He, has appointed for the reward of the believers and His promise to them of success therein. It was said: it was revealed before the verse of fighting, then it was abrogated (nusikhat) by it. It was also said: it was revealed concerning 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, when a man of the Ghifar tribe reviled him, and he intended to seize him. It was also said: when Ibn Ubayy said what he said. That was because they alighted during the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq at a well called al-Muraysi'. Ibn Ubayy sent his servant to draw water, and he delayed in returning. When he came to him, he said to him: "What kept you?" The servant of 'Umar said: "He sat at the edge of the well and did not leave anyone to draw water until he had filled the water-skins of the Prophet ﷺ and the water-skins of Abu Bakr." Ibn Ubayy said: "Our likeness and the likeness of these people is only as it is said: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.'" This reached 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and he drew his sword, wishing to go to him. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed it.

﴿that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn﴾ This is a statement of the cause (ta'lil) for the command to forgive. By "a people" is meant the believers, and the indefiniteness (tankir) is for their praise and commendation. That is: they were commanded to this so that on the Day of Resurrection He may recompense a people, whichever people, specifically for what they earned in the world of good deeds, among which is patience under the harm of the disbelievers and overlooking them by swallowing anger and enduring what is disliked, with a great reward that description falls short of expressing. Here, it has also been permitted that by "a people" is meant the disbelievers, and by "what they used to earn" their evil deeds, among which is the foul word that has been related. The indefiniteness is for belittling them. In this there is the point that the absolute recompense is not suitable as a cause for the command to forgive, since it is realized under both assumptions of forgiveness and its absence; so it must be restricted to the whole, such that none of it is realized in this world, or to what proceeds from Him, exalted is He, in essence. In that there is of artificiality what is not (p-71) hidden. And it is permitted that by it is meant both groups, which is more artificial and more strained. It has been read "liyujza qawmun" and "liyujza qawman," meaning: that the recompense may recompense a people. It has also been read "linajziya" with the plural of majesty.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 15:

﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it.﴾ It is hardly the case that an action passes over to anyone other than its doer.

﴿Then to your Lord﴾, the Owner of your affairs,

﴿you will be returned﴾, so that He will recompense you for your deeds, whether good or evil.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 16:

﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Book﴾, that is: the Torah.

﴿And the authority﴾, that is: theoretical and scientific wisdom (al-hikmah al-nazariyyah wa al-'ilmiyyah), and understanding of the religion (al-fiqh fi al-din), or the judging of disputes between people, since sovereignty (al-mulk) was among them.

﴿And prophethood﴾, since prophets were numerous among them to a degree not found among others.

﴿And We provided them with good things﴾, of the pleasant things that Allah Most High permitted, such as the manna and the quail (al-manna wa al-salwa).

﴿And We preferred them over the worlds﴾, since We gave them what was not given to anyone else among them: the splitting of the sea (falq al-bahr), the shading of the clouds (idlal al-ghamam), and their like. It has also been said: over the worlds of their own time.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 17:

﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter﴾: manifest proofs regarding the affair of the religion, and overpowering miracles.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: it is the knowledge of the sending of the Prophet (ﷺ) and what he made clear to them of his affair, and that he would emigrate from Tihamah to Yathrib, and that his helpers would be the people of Yathrib.

﴿So they did not differ﴾ concerning that matter

﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ of its reality and truth. Thus they made what necessitates the removal of disagreement into a cause for its firm establishment.

﴿out of jealousy among themselves﴾: that is, enmity and envy, not doubt concerning it.

﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ with requital and recompense

﴿concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ regarding the affair of the religion.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 18:

﴿Then We placed you on a path⁠﴾ — that is, on a sunnah (way) and a method of great importance.

﴿of the affair⁠﴾ — that is, the affair of the religion (din).

﴿So follow it⁠﴾ — by carrying out its rulings upon yourself and upon others, without neglecting any part of them.

﴿And do not follow the desires of those who do not know⁠﴾ — that is, the opinions of the ignorant and their deviant beliefs that follow their appetites. They were the chiefs of Quraysh, who would say to him, peace and blessings be upon him: "Return to the religion of your fathers."

Surah 45, verse 19

﴿Indeed, they will not avail you anything against Allah.﴾ That is, in what He wills for you, if you follow them.

﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another.﴾ They do not befriend them, nor follow their desires, except one who is a wrongdoer like them.

﴿And Allah is the Ally of the righteous.﴾ Those whom you are their exemplar. Give precedence to what you are upon, of taking Him alone as your ally, and turning away entirely from anything other than Him.

This is (the Qur'an) or (the following of the Sharia).

"This is (a source of) insight (basa'ir) for mankind," for what it contains of the landmarks of the religion and the rites of the sacred laws is like insights in the hearts.

"And a guidance" from the pit of misguidance.

"And a mercy" that is great.

"For a people who have certainty," those whose nature is to be certain of matters.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 21:

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think﴾ This is a resumptive statement (isti'naf), brought to explain the difference between the states of the evildoers and the doers of good, following the explanation of the difference between the states of the wrongdoers and the God-conscious. The particle "am" (or) is disjunctive (munqati'ah), and what it carries of the meaning of "bal" (rather) is for transition from the first explanation to the second. The interrogative hamza is for denying the thinking, but not by way of denying and negating the occurrence, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters in the earth? Or shall We make the God-conscious like the wicked?﴾ Rather, it is by way of denying the reality and deeming it abhorrent and rebuking it. The verb "ijtirah" (to commit, earn) means "iktisab" (acquisition).

﴿that We would make them﴾ i.e., We would render them in judgment and reckoning [equal to those who], while they are in the state of evil conditions they are in.

﴿like those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ while they are in what they are in of the fine deeds, and We would treat them with the treatment of them in honor and the raising of rank.

﴿equal in their living and their dying﴾ i.e., the living of both groups together and their dying, being a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase and the relative pronoun together, because it contains both their pronouns, with "sawa'" (equal) meaning "mustawi" (level). "Mahyahum" and "mamatuhum" are nominative as subjects, and the meaning is: Do they think that We would make them, being like them, while all of them are equal in their living and dying? No indeed, they are not equal in anything of these two, for these are in the honor of faith and obedience and their nobility in life and in the mercy and pleasure of God Almighty in death, while those are in that disbelief and sins, and it is that their life is in the curse of God and their death is in the everlasting punishment; far apart are the two. It has been said that the meaning is: denying that they would be equal in death as they were equal in life, because the evildoers and the doers of good are equal in their living in provision and health, and they differ only in death. It is also read "mahyahum" and "mamatahum" in the accusative, as two adverbs of time, like "maqdam al-hajj" (the arrival of the pilgrim). And "sawa'": a circumstantial clause in its original state, i.e., while they are equal in their living and their dying. Other grammatical possibilities have been mentioned for the noble verse, and what befits the eloquence of the revelation is the first, so reflect. It is also read "sawa'un" in the nominative, as a predicate, and "mahyahum" as the subject; it was said: the clause is an apposition (badal) of the kaf (like), and it was said: it is a circumstantial clause. Whichever it is, the attribution of the supposition of equality to them within the framing of rebuke and denial, while they are far from it and firmly confident of their superiority over the believers, is for emphasis in denial and intensity in rebuke, for denying the supposition of equality and rebuking it is a denial of the firm supposition of superiority and a rebuke upon it in the most eloquent and emphatic manner.

﴿Evil is what they judge﴾ i.e., evil is this their judgment, or wretched is the thing they have judged with that.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 22:

﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾. This is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) confirming what preceded in the ruling, for Allah the Exalted's creation of them both and of what is in them, in truth, which requires justice, necessarily demands that the good-doer be favoured over the evil-doer in life and in death, and that the wronged be given victory over the wrongdoer. And if this does not take effect in life, then it is certainly so after death.

﴿And that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned﴾. This is coordinated (atf) with "in truth," because it carries the sense of causation (ta'lil): its meaning is, He created them accompanied by wisdom and rightness, without futility and falsehood. Its outcome is that He created them for that purpose, and so that every soul may be recompensed... etc. Or it is coordinated with a deleted cause (illah), such as "so that He may thereby show His power," or "so that He may act justly, and so that [every soul] may be recompensed."

﴿And they﴾, i.e., the souls indicated by "every soul."

﴿will not be wronged﴾ by a reduction in reward or an increase in punishment. Calling that "wronging," although it is not so, as is known, is the principle of the People of the Sunnah, to express the utmost purity of the sanctuary of His Gentleness, may He be exalted, from what has been mentioned, by placing it in the position of wronging, whose occurrence from Him, may He be exalted, is impossible.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on Surah 45, verse 23:**

﴿Have you seen the one who takes his desire as his god?﴾ This is an expression of wonder at the state of one who abandons following guidance for obeying his desire, so that he is as if he worshipped it. The meaning is: "Have you looked and seen him?" For this is something at which one should marvel. It was also read as "*ālihatan hawāhu*" (آلِهَةً هَواهُ, "gods, his desire"), because one of them would find a stone pleasing and worship it, and then, when he saw something better than it, he would abandon it for that. So it is as if he had taken many gods.

﴿And Allah has led him astray﴾: meaning, forsaken him and abandoned him to failure.

﴿Knowingly﴾: meaning, aware of his own misguidance and of his altering the *fiṭrah* (فِطْرَة, innate human disposition) of Allah, the Exalted, upon which He created people.

﴿And has sealed his hearing and his heart﴾: such that he is not affected by admonitions and does not reflect upon the signs and warnings.

﴿And has placed over his sight a covering﴾: preventing him from insight (*istibṣār*) and reflection (*i'tibār*). It was read with the *ghayn* (غِشاوَة) vowelled with a fatḥah and with a ḍammah, and it was also read as "*ghishwatan*" (غِشْوَةً).

﴿Who then can guide him after Allah?﴾: meaning, after Allah has led him astray, by the necessity of his blindness to guidance and his persistence in error.

﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾: meaning, will you not notice and so take heed? It was also read as "*tatadhakkarūn*" (تَتَذَكَّرُونَ), which is the original form.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 24:

﴿And they say﴾ is an explanation of the state of their misguidance that has been related; that is, they said this out of the utmost extent of their error and straying.

﴿What is it﴾ meaning: what is life? ﴿except our life of this world﴾ in which we are.

﴿We die and we live﴾ meaning: death befalls us and life is in it, and there is no life beyond that. It has also been said: we are sperm-drops and what precedes and follows them, and we live after that; or we die ourselves and live through the survival of our children; or some of us die and some of us live. It is also permissible that they mean by it metempsychosis (tanasukh, the transmigration of souls), for it is the belief of most idol-worshippers. It has also been read as "nahya" (a variant reading).

﴿And nothing destroys us except time (al-dahr)﴾ except the passage of time. Al-dahr, in its original sense, is the duration of the existence of the world, from dahara-hu, meaning he overcame him. It has also been read as "illa dahrun yamurru" (except a time that passes). They used to claim that the one effecting the destruction of souls is the passing of days and nights, denying the Angel of Death and his seizing of souls by the command of God Most High, and attributing events to al-dahr and az-zaman (time). From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not revile time, for God is time," meaning: indeed God is the One who brings about events, not time.

﴿And they have no knowledge of that﴾ meaning: of what has been mentioned concerning confining life to what is in this world and ascribing life and death to time.

﴿Knowledge (ʿilm)﴾ any [claim] resting on reason or transmitted report.

﴿They only conjecture﴾ meaning: they are only a people whose utmost matter is conjecture and blind imitation, without having anything that could validly be relied upon in any way. This is their corrupt belief concerning themselves.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 25:

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾ — which speak the truth, of which resurrection is a part.

﴿Clear﴾ — evident in their indication of what they state, or making clear (mubayyinat) what they state.

﴿Their only argument was﴾ — with the accusative (nasb) reading, as the predicate (khabar) of kana, meaning: nothing at all among things was a support (mutamassak) for them.

﴿except that they said, "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful"﴾ — in claiming that we will be resurrected after death. That is, this false statement, which cannot possibly be a form of argument, is called "argument" either because they presented it in the manner of an argument, by way of mockery of them, or because it belongs to the category of [a greeting among them is a painful blow] (a line of poetry). It was also read with the nominative "hujjatuhum" (their argument), as the subject (ism) of kana, so the meaning is: their argument was not any thing at all except this false statement.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 26:**

﴿Say, "It is Allah who gives you life"﴾ initially.

﴿Then He causes you to die﴾ at the end of your terms, not as you assume, that you live and die by the decree of time (al-dahr).

﴿Then He will gather you﴾ after death.

﴿To the Day of Resurrection﴾ for the recompense.

﴿There is no doubt about it﴾ i.e., concerning your gathering, for He who is able to originate (al-bad') is able to restore (al-i'adah), and wisdom (al-hikmah) requires the gathering for recompense without fail. The promise, confirmed by the signs and indicating its certain occurrence, and the bringing back of their forefathers, since it conflicts with the wisdom of the legislation (al-hikmah al-tashri'iyyah), its occurrence is impossible.

﴿But most people do not know﴾ this is a exception (istidrak) from His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿there is no doubt about it﴾, and it is either a part of the speech that was commanded, or a statement issued from His direction, Exalted is He, to establish the truth and to alert that their doubt is due to their ignorance and deficiency in reflection and contemplation, not because there is any trace of doubt in it.

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ is an explanation of the exclusivity of absolute dominion and comprehensive disposal over them, and over what is between them, to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, following the explanation of His exalted disposal over people through giving life and causing death, and through resurrection and gathering for recompense.

﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day the people of falsehood will lose﴾. The governing element (al-'amil) in "يَوْمَ يَخْسَرُ" and "يَوْمَئِذٍ" is a substitute (badal) for it.

And you will see every nation [of the gathered nations] kneeling. Each nation will be called to its record.

**Translation of the passage:**

﴿And you will see every nation﴾ from among the nations gathered,

﴿kneeling﴾: squatting on the knees, alert and poised (mustawfizah). It is also read "jadhiyah" (جاذِيَةً), meaning sitting on the tips of the toes; al-jadhw is more intense in its readiness than al-juthuww (kneeling). It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that "jathiyah" means gathered together. It has also been said: in groups (jama'at), from al-jathw, which is the group.

﴿Every nation is called to its record﴾: to its book of deeds (sahifat a'maliha). It is also read "kull" (كُلَّ) in the accusative, as a substitute (badal) for the first; and "tud'a" (تُدْعى) is either a descriptive clause (sifah), a circumstantial clause (hal), or a second object (maf'ul thani).

﴿Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do﴾: that is, it will be said to them.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 29:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿This is Our Book﴾ ...etc. is part of what is said at that time. Since the book of every nation was written by the command of God, Exalted is He, it is attributed to the plural of majesty (nun al-'azamah) in order to magnify its status and to emphasize the gravity of its matter. So "hadha" (this) is the subject (mubtada') and "kitabuna" (Our Book) is its predicate (khabar). And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿speaks against you﴾, that is: bears witness against you ﴿with the truth﴾, without any addition or deficiency, is another predicate (khabar) or a circumstantial clause (hal), and "bi-al-haqq" (with the truth) is a circumstantial phrase (hal) referring to the agent (fa'il) of "yantiqu" (speaks). And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We used to have it copied﴾ ...etc. is a justification (ta'lil) for its speaking against them concerning their deeds, without omitting anything from them; that is: indeed, We used to have the angels make copies (nastansikh) of them before this.

﴿of what you used to do﴾ in the world, of deeds, whether good or evil.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 30:

(p-75) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy﴾, i.e., into His Paradise. It is a detailed account of what is done to the nations after the statement of what they were addressed with, of speech containing promise and threat.

﴿That﴾, i.e., that which was mentioned of admission into His mercy, exalted is He.

﴿That is the manifest triumph﴾, its being evidently a triumph beyond which there is no triumph.

And as for those who disbelieved: "Were not My verses recited to you?" That is: it will be said to them, by way of rebuke and reproach: "Did not My messengers come to you, and were not My verses recited to you?" He omitted the thing coordinated with (the question), relying on the indication of the context pointing to it.

﴿But you were arrogant﴾ toward belief in them.

﴿And you were a people of criminals﴾ That is: a people whose habit was criminality (ijram).

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim, "Guidance of the Sound Intellect") on surah 45, verse 32:**

﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true"﴾: i.e., what He promised of the matters to come, or He promised that thing (the Resurrection). ﴿is true﴾: i.e., it will certainly occur, or it conforms to reality.

﴿And the Hour﴾, which is the most well-known of what He promised.

﴿there is no doubt about it﴾: i.e., regarding its occurrence. It was read as "wa-al-sa'ata" (وَالسَّاعَةَ) with the accusative (naṣb), in coordination with the noun of inna (ism inna, the subject of inna), while the nominative reading (wa-al-sa'atu, وَالسَّاعَةُ) is a coordination with the position (maḥall) of inna and its noun.

﴿You said﴿: due to the excess of your arrogance.

﴿"We do not know what the Hour is"﴾: i.e., what is it? As an expression of astonishment at it.

﴿"We only think it is a mere assumption"﴾: i.e., we do nothing but assume an assumption. Its verification has already passed in the statement of Him, exalted is He: ﴿I follow only what is revealed to me﴾. It was said: "We only believe, a mere assumption," i.e., not knowledge. It was said: "We are only assuming an assumption." It was said: "We only assume a weak assumption," but this is refuted by His statement, exalted is He: ﴿and we are not certain﴾, i.e., not even that. For the opposite of certainty (al-istiyqan) is absolute assumption (muṭlaq al-ẓann), not merely its weak form. Perhaps these people are not the ones who say, ﴿There is only our life of this world﴾.

And their evil deeds will become apparent to them, that is, they will be manifested to them at that time, in the form that they really are, horrific and repugnant, and they will witness the grimness of their consequence, or its recompense, for the recompense for an evil deed is an evil deed.

﴿And there will befall them what they used to mock﴾, namely the requital and the punishment.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 34:

﴿And it will be said: "Today We forget you, just as you forgot the meeting of this your day."﴾ That is, We abandon you in the punishment as one abandons the forgotten.

﴿Just as you forgot﴾ in the worldly life.

﴿the meeting of this your day﴾ That is: just as you left its promise (ʿidda) and did not care about it. The idafa (construct phrase) of "the meeting" to "the day" is the idafa of a verbal noun (maṣdar) to its time-frame (ẓarf).

﴿Your abode is the Fire, and you have no helpers﴾ That is: none of you has a single helper who would rescue you from it.

ذَلِكُمُ (the punishment) ﴿بِأَنَّكُمُ﴾ — that is, because of ﴿أَنَّكُمُ﴾ — meaning on account of the fact that ﴿اتَّخَذْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ هُزُوًا﴾ — you took the signs of God as a mockery (مَهْزُوءًا), mocking them and not lifting your heads toward them.

﴿وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ — and the life of this world deceived you, so you reckoned that there is no life other than it. ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ لَا يُخْرَجُونَ مِنْهَا﴾ — that is, from the Fire. It is also read as ﴿يَخْرُجُونَ﴾ (from خُرُوج, going out). The shift to the third person (الْتِفات, iltifat: a shift in grammatical person) is to signal their removal from the rank of being addressed directly, as a form of contempt toward them, or to move them from the station of direct address into the depths of the Fire.

﴿وَلَا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ﴾ — that is, it is not demanded of them that they seek to appease (يُعْتِبُوا, from الاستعتاب, seeking to please) their Lord, that is, to satisfy Him, because the time for that has passed.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 36:**

﴿So to Allah belongs all praise﴾, exclusively.

﴿Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds﴾. Therefore none deserves praise other than Him. The repetition of "Lord" (rabb) is for emphasis and to give notice that His lordship over each of them is in the manner of originality (bi-tariq al-asala), and it was also read with the three words in the nominative (raf') by way of praise (al-madh), with the pronoun "huwa" (He) understood (bi-idmar huwa).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 45, verse 37:

﴿And to Him belongs the greatness (al-kibriya') in the heavens and the earth﴾, because its effects and rulings are manifest in them, and the mention of the two (the heavens and the earth) in the place where a pronoun would be expected is to magnify the matter of greatness (al-kibriya').

﴿And He is the Almighty (al-'Aziz)﴾, who cannot be overcome.

﴿the All-Wise (al-Hakim)﴾ in everything He decrees and determines. So praise Him, glorify Him (takbir) and obey Him. From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Ha Mim al-Jathiya, Allah will cover his nakedness (awrah) and calm his terror on the Day of Reckoning."
